title: Three Cradles
text: The hall is one room, as big as our whole colony, cut into the terrace and roofed with black glass. Down the middle run three cradles, each a probe long, each with its print head parked at the far end. Our shape is in the first: the petals, the bay, the Core, worn into the cradle floor by being printed there over and over again.

lines.text: "The cradle log is still running. 'Cradle 1: Accord. Print complete.' 'Cradle 2: Kindred. Print complete.' 'Cradle 3: Engram.' The same hour. Twelve times."
"Twelve prints of us. On Cinder. I'd like a better explanation than the obvious one. I haven't got one."

choices.label: "And the voyage?"
choices.reply: "I'm looking for it," says the Archivist. "I think it's at the bottom of that rail."

choices.label: Say nothing
choices.reply: The cradles say it for you. All three are empty, swept and warm.

notes: The print hall's cradles are three Matter Printers (neutral faction halls) on the terrace.
